title: brief=only skips the fair-use limit: on a cache miss it runs a full check and ignores the count, and on a cache hit it asks the models without limit
evidence: Temporary test: 60 POSTs {name:'Jane Doe', company:'Acme<i>', brief:'only'} from one address returned 60 x 200 and 0 x 429, with 60 runFounderBrief calls. The signed-out limit is 15 per 10 minutes. Line 170 calls countHit but never uses its result.
scenario: A script sends brief:'only' with a new company each time. Every call misses the cache, so runFounderBrief runs the whole check (6-12 metered searches plus up to 3 parallel model calls). None is refused. Line 170 counts the hit but never checks the returned wait. With a cache hit, repeated brief:'only' calls ask the models again for 10 minutes and are not counted at all.
fix: On a cache miss, call countHit before the run, the same way as the other modes, and return 429 when it says to wait. On a cache hit, allow one brief per cached state: delete the entry or mark it used after writeBrief, or count 'only' calls in a separate small window (for example 3 per state). A repeat with no state left then counts as a new check.
verifyNote: index.js skips countHit for mode 'only'. On a cache miss it counts only after the full run and throws the result away, so the call is never refused. recallState never consumes the entry, so cache hits call the models again for 10 minutes without being counted.
betterFix: On a miss, run the same countHit (owner plus 'everyone') before runFounderBrief and return 429 when it says to wait. On a hit, take the state out of the cache in runFounderBrief: delete the key, or set a 'briefed' flag and fall through to a counted full check. Then one counted check yields exactly one model brief.

title: When several people share the name, their timeline, litigation and press are returned unflagged and shown under the chooser as one person's
evidence: runFounderCheck('John Kowalczyk', no company) with pages for a pastor at Grace Chapel and an Acme CEO: people has 2 groups and briefInfo.mode is 'choose'. Litigation returns the pastor's 'sued over fraud' items with no possibleDifferentPerson flag. founder.js renders {quickBrief} sections whenever choosing is true.
scenario: An investor types 'Michael Smith' with no company. The server writes no brief and returns `people`, but `other` and `weak` stay empty on this branch. Every evidence list mixes all the namesakes with no flag. The page shows the Chooser and, below it, Litigation and Timeline sections that put a pastor's fraud lawsuit under the founder's name.
fix: In the people branch, set `x.group` and `x.possibleDifferentPerson = true` on every evidence item (or return the lists grouped by `groupOf`). Better still, send no timeline, litigation, press, companies or education until a person is chosen, and return only the people list and sources. In founder.js, hide the quickBrief sections while `choosing && !nameAlone`.
verifyNote: Reproduced: the people branch returns mode 'choose' with the pastor's 'sued for fraud' items and no possibleDifferentPerson or nameOnly flag. founder.js renders quickBrief (Timeline, Litigation, Press) whenever data exists. Only the network panel is gated on !choosing, so the namesakes' items show under the Chooser.
betterFix: In gatherSources' people branch, mark every evidence item with its group from groupOf and set possibleDifferentPerson on all of them. In founder.js, render only the sources card while choosing && !nameAlone. After 'name alone', show the items under OwnThenOthers as unconfirmed.

title: No company typed and one group 'dominant': name-only pages (any namesake) go into the quoted brief's Litigation and Press as the person's own; nameOnly is never read
evidence: Pages: 1 'John Kowalczyk, CEO of Acme' and 3 with no affiliation, one of them 'Man named John Kowalczyk charged with fraud'. Result: people=null; the quoted brief says 'most of them place John Kowalczyk at Acme'; LITIGATION quotes the robbery charge; PRESS lists the marathon page. Items carry nameOnly:true, which no UI file reads (grep).
scenario: When a single group exists, `dominant` is true even for a group of 1 among 15 name-only pages. Those pages go into `weak`, not `other`, so quotedBrief's `mine` filter keeps them. A namesake's criminal charge is listed under LITIGATION AND REGULATORY, the summary claims 'most of them' place the person at the one company found, and the page's sections show the same items unmarked.
fix: Require the top group to cover a real share of the ranked pages (for example at least 3 pages and at least 40%). Otherwise return `people` or treat everything as name-only. In quotedBrief, leave weak items out of LITIGATION, RED FLAGS and the 'most of them' sentence, or list them under a 'name only, may be someone else' sub-heading. Have founder.js treat nameOnly like possibleDifferentPerson in OwnThenOthers.
verifyNote: Reproduced: one Acme profile plus three unaffiliated pages gives dominant=true because there is no second group. The quoted brief says 'most of them place John Kowalczyk at Acme' and lists 'charged with fraud after a robbery' under LITIGATION and TIMELINE. nameOnly is never read by the UI.
betterFix: For !second, require at least DOMINANT_MIN members and at least 40% of the grouped plus weak pages; otherwise treat every page as name-only. In quotedBrief, filter weak indexes out of litigation and the summary claim, or list them under 'name only, may be someone else'. In OwnThenOthers, treat nameOnly like possibleDifferentPerson.

title: The line check accepts a made-up conviction: lower-case legal claims need only any valid citation
evidence: checkFounderBrief: 'She was convicted of wire fraud and sentenced to prison [Source 1]' under LITIGATION, citing a LinkedIn profile source with no legal words, plus 'She was charged with securities fraud [Source 2]' under RED FLAGS. Result: ok:true, dropped 0, confidence High.
scenario: A model draws on outside knowledge, or mixes up a namesake, and writes 'He was convicted of fraud [Source 3]' where Source 3 is a funding article. supports() checks only years, numbers and capitalised names, and the person's own name is ignored, so the line has nothing to check and passes. The page shows a cited criminal conviction that no source states.
fix: In checkClaims, add an option such as `legalTerms`: any sentence matching founderCheck's LEGAL_STRONG/LEGAL_WEAK/LEGAL_AGENCY (in every section, not only LITIGATION) must cite a source whose text also matches a legal term from the same family (convicted, charged, sued, fraud and so on). Otherwise drop it, and fail the answer when it sits under LITIGATION. Pass it from checkFounderBrief only, so Open Research is unchanged.
verifyNote: Reproduced: 'She was convicted of wire fraud and sentenced to prison [Source 1]' under LITIGATION, citing a LinkedIn profile, passes with ok:true and 0 dropped. supports() checks only years, numbers and capitalised names, and the sentence-initial 'She' is skipped.
betterFix: Add a legalTerms option to checkClaims, passed only from checkFounderBrief: a sentence in any section with a LEGAL_STRONG, LEGAL_AGENCY or LEGAL_WEAK term must cite a non-weak source that also contains a legal term. Fail the answer when this happens under LITIGATION, drop the sentence elsewhere. Open Research is unchanged.

title: A namesake's legal matter from a name-only source passes when the model puts it in SUMMARY, TIMELINE or PRESS
evidence: checkFounderBrief with source 2 weak:true: 'He was charged with fraud after a robbery [Source 2]' in SUMMARY and 'Police said he was charged with fraud [Source 2]' in PRESS. Result: ok:true, while LITIGATION says no litigation was found.
scenario: No company typed, dominant group, so the unaffiliated pages go to the model marked match="name only". weakDropSections covers only LITIGATION and RED FLAGS. The model writes the namesake's charge in the SUMMARY. It is kept, and the brief contradicts itself ('no litigation found').
fix: Drop any sentence that cites only weak sources and contains a legal term, in every section. Or add SUMMARY and CAREER TIMELINE to weakDropSections for legal-term lines, and treat a dropped legal line as a failure of the answer.
verifyNote: Reproduced: 'She was charged with fraud [Source 2]' in SUMMARY, where source 2 is weak and does not even mention fraud, is kept with ok:true while LITIGATION says not found. weakDropSections covers only LITIGATION and RED FLAGS.
betterFix: Covered by the legalTerms rule if it requires a non-weak legal source. Separately, drop any sentence in any section whose only citations are weak and that contains a legal term, and count such a drop toward failing the answer.

title: With a company typed, court dockets naming the person are filtered out as namesakes, and the quoted brief then says no litigation was found
evidence: runFounderCheck('John Smith', company 'Ramp') with a CourtListener result 'JOHN SMITH, Plaintiff v. RAMP BUSINESS CORP' names the person: it lands in namesakePages, and litigation is []. RECAP dockets almost never name the employer next to the person.
scenario: An investor checks Trevor Milton / Nikola, and CourtListener returns 'United States v. Milton' with no 'Nikola' near the name. tiedByCompany is false, so the docket is left out. The quoted brief prints 'No litigation or regulatory mentions found in the available sources.' The only trace is a generic left-out count in the notes.
fix: Keep CourtListener results whose title or snippet names the person in full as name-only (weak) rather than dropping them, or at least count them. In the LITIGATION section of both briefs, say 'N court records name a <name> but not <company>; they were left out and may be about someone else'. Never print a plain 'none found' when such records exist.
verifyNote: With a company typed, tiedByCompany needs the company near the name, which RECAP dockets rarely give. They go to namesakePages, and LITIGATION prints 'Not found' plus the generic disclaimer. Only a generic left-out page count hints at them. Leaving them out is right; staying silent about court records is not.
betterFix: Keep the exclusion, since wrong-person is the worse failure. Count the left-out courtlistener results separately, return them as namesakeCourtRecords, and have both briefs' LITIGATION say 'N court records name a <name> without <company>; they were left out and may or may not be this person' instead of a plain 'not found'.

title: The cross-site guard covers GET only: a text/plain POST from any site runs checks counted against the visitor's address
evidence: Read: the Sec-Fetch-Site test is gated on req.method === 'GET'. input() parses a string body with safeJson, so a no-cors fetch with Content-Type text/plain (a simple request, no preflight) is accepted.
scenario: A third-party page runs fetch('/api/founder', {method:'POST', mode:'no-cors', body:'{"name":"Jane Doe"}'}) in each visitor's browser. Each visit spends searches and models and uses up that visitor's per-address allowance. Many visitors can also drain the 600/hour 'everyone' cap, which locks out every signed-out user.
fix: Refuse any method when sec-fetch-site is 'cross-site'. Accept POST only with Content-Type application/json, which forces a preflight from another origin, and drop the string-body JSON parsing.
verifyNote: The Sec-Fetch-Site guard is gated on GET, and input() JSON-parses a string body. A no-cors text/plain POST from another site therefore runs a counted check, spending the visitor's allowance and the shared 'everyone' cap.
betterFix: Refuse sec-fetch-site 'cross-site' for every method. For POST, require Content-Type application/json, which forces a preflight from another origin, and drop the safeJson parsing of string bodies.

title: The quick brief keeps wedding and spouse headlines that the deep check drops
evidence: cleanSearchResult titles: 'Trevor Milton marries Carrie Smith in Utah' and 'Trevor Milton and wife Carrie Milton donate to hospital' come back unchanged. sanitizeFinding in guardrails.js drops a title matching WEDDING_TITLE.
scenario: A search result headline about the person's marriage or spouse goes to the model prompt, into Press and Mentions, and into the Sources list. The same record would be removed in the deep check.
fix: In cleanSearchResult, drop the result when WEDDING_TITLE (export it from guardrails) or the family-notice part of privacyReason(title, { kin: 'notices' }) matches the title, the same way sanitizeFinding does.
verifyNote: Reproduced: cleanSearchResult keeps 'Trevor Milton weds Carrie Smith', which the deep check's WEDDING_TITLE drops. The reviewer's examples 'marries' and 'wife' match neither path, so the deep check misses them too.
betterFix: Export WEDDING_TITLE from guardrails and drop a result in cleanSearchResult when its title matches, as sanitizeFinding does. Also extend WEDDING_TITLE (in both paths) to marries, married, and 'and (his|her) (wife|husband)' so spouse headlines are removed consistently.

title: The fallback digest names junk companies and roles read from headlines
scenario: Preview, real search results, no model: "Career: 3 companies named in the sources (Brex, Stealth, Founding Story The)"; "Career: 5 companies (Ramp, Nearly, Companies, Top)"; "Most recent role found: CEO at Who Is Canva"; "Most recent role found: co-founders at Ramp"; a quote starting "[email removed] Eric Glyman is..."; a quote that is an Instagram caption "May be an image of text.]".
fix: A company in the digest must come from a profile field or a sentence about the person, never from capitalised headline words; drop "Most recent role" unless the company is the typed one or a profile field; strip removal markers and image-caption boilerplate from quotes; prefer the résumé lines of founder/profile.js over these heuristics.
